Package com.google.mu.protobuf.util

Class MoreStructs

java.lang.Object
com.google.mu.protobuf.util.MoreStructs
@CheckReturnValue public final class MoreStructs extends Object
Additional utilities to help create Struct and Value messages.

Since Struct fields map to dynamically typed values, throughout this class, struct values of all supported types (numeric, string, boolean, null) and the Collections, Maps, Tables, Optionals thereof are automatically converted to their corresponding Value wrappers. This allows users to more conveniently create Struct and Value.

Occasionally, an application may need custom logic to convert a domain-specific type into Value, and then recursively into ListValue and/or Struct. This can be done by implementing ValueConverter.

Since:
5.8

    static com.google.protobuf.Value
    toValue(Object object)
    Converts object to Value according to the following rules: Primitive types (numbers, strings, booleans) and Struct proto types (Struct, ListValue etc.) are wrapped inside the respective Value wrapper protos; null and NullValue are converted to NullValue; Value is returned as is; Optional of primitive types, Value or struct proto types is unwrapped then converted, with the empty() instance converted to NullValue; Collection (Iterable, Map, Multimap, Table)s are recursively converted.

    • toStruct

      public static <T> Collector<T,?,com.google.protobuf.Struct> toStruct(Function<? super T,? extends CharSequence> toKey, Function<? super T,?> toValue)
      Returns a Collector that accumulates elements into a Struct whose keys and values are the result of applying the provided mapping functions to the input elements.

      Duplicate keys (according to Object.equals(Object)) are not allowed.

      Null keys are not allowed, but null values are represented with NullValue.

    • toStruct

      public static BiCollector<CharSequence,Object,com.google.protobuf.Struct> toStruct()
      Returns a BiCollector that accumulates the name-value pairs into a Struct with the values converted using toValue(java.lang.Object).

      Duplicate keys (according to Object.equals(Object)) are not allowed.

      Null keys are not allowed, but null values will be represented with NullValue.

      Can also be used to create Struct literals conveniently, such as: 

      
 BiStream.of("foo", 1. "bar", true).collect(toStruct());

    • toValue

      public static com.google.protobuf.Value toValue(Object object)
      Converts object to Value according to the following rules:
      • Primitive types (numbers, strings, booleans) and Struct proto types (Struct, ListValue etc.) are wrapped inside the respective Value wrapper protos;
      • null and NullValue are converted to NullValue;
      • Value is returned as is;
      • Optional of primitive types, Value or struct proto types is unwrapped then converted, with the empty() instance converted to NullValue;
      • Collection (Iterable, Map, Multimap, Table)s are recursively converted. Specifically:
        • Iterable is wrapped as ListValue;
        • Map is wrapped as Struct;
        • Multimap is wrapped as Struct with all values mapped to the same key wrapped inside a ListValue.
        • Table is wrapped as a Struct with string to Struct mappings; 
      
 maps.stream()
     .map(MoreStructs::toValue)
     .collect(toListValue());
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if object cannot be converted to Value.
